title: Unified Model Routing for Global Content Aggregators
business: A global content aggregator platform that dynamically generates summaries for diverse international news feeds.
problem: The platform suffers from vendor lock-in and high latency when specific model providers experience service outages or capacity constraints, forcing manual code changes to switch endpoints.
solution: By integrating the OpenRouter API, the platform gains access to hundreds of AI models through a single endpoint, allowing the application to switch between providers or utilize model aliases like ~openai/gpt-sol-latest to ensure continuous service without redeploying code.
steps: Register for an OpenRouter API key to authenticate requests.
Configure the application to point to the OpenRouter base URL instead of individual provider endpoints.
Implement model aliases (e.g., ~openai/gpt-sol-latest) in the request payload to automatically resolve to the freshest model version.
Add optional headers like X-OpenRouter-Title to track usage and attribution within the OpenRouter ecosystem.
outcome: The platform achieves high availability and operational agility, as the unified interface abstracts away the underlying provider infrastructure, enabling seamless model swapping.
limitation: A significant trade-off is the reliance on a single intermediary; if the OpenRouter gateway experiences downtime, all connected model integrations will fail simultaneously. This can be checked by monitoring the health of the OpenRouter API endpoint versus individual provider status pages.

questions.question: In Unified Model Routing for Global Content Aggregators, how does the solution address the problem of vendor lock-in?
options: By forcing the use of a single proprietary model provider.
By providing access to hundreds of models through a single API endpoint.
By requiring manual code changes for every model update.
By eliminating the need for any AI model providers.
questions.explanation: The solution leverages OpenRouter's ability to provide access to hundreds of models via one endpoint, removing the need to hardcode specific provider logic.
questions.evidence: By integrating the OpenRouter API, the platform gains access to hundreds of AI models through a single endpoint, allowing the application to switch between providers or utilize model aliases like ~openai/gpt-sol-latest to ensure continuous service without redeploying code.

options: The system requires constant manual updates to the API key.
The system cannot use model aliases for routing.
The platform becomes dependent on the OpenRouter gateway for all model requests.
The system is unable to track usage or attribution.
questions.explanation: Centralizing through OpenRouter creates a single point of failure where the gateway's status dictates the availability of all underlying models.
